meta.title: COHO market patterns and a Colorado strategy menu
meta.generated_at_note: the market-direction stamp this was built from, not the time this ran

resort.label: Resort and second-home
resort.rule: Seasonal homes are 20% or more of all homes (ACS), or the market call is "second-home shift".
resort.plain: Many homes sit empty part of the year, so workers compete with buyers who do not live here.

job_centre.label: Job centre
job_centre.rule: 2,000 or more jobs and at least 1.3 jobs for every working resident (LODES).
job_centre.plain: More people come in to work than live here, so the need reaches workers who live elsewhere.

growing.label: Fast-growing
growing.rule: Household population up 2% or more a year, or the market call is "emerging".
growing.plain: Households are arriving quickly, so land and approvals are the pinch points.

softening.label: Softening or shrinking
softening.rule: The market call is "softening" or "falling demand", or household population is down 0.5% or more a year.
softening.plain: Prices, permits or people are slipping, so keeping and fixing existing homes goes further than building.

steady.label: Steady
steady.rule: None of the rules above holds.
steady.plain: No strong push either way, so a standard tax credit deal sized to local need is the usual route.

too_little_data.label: Too little data
too_little_data.rule: No market call and no household population reading.
too_little_data.plain: Public data is too thin to type this place. The county type is shown instead.

resort.why: Buying deed restrictions on existing homes keeps them for local workers without new land.
Visitors and short-term rentals can help pay for worker housing, with voter approval.
Land is the scarce input here, so public and banked land does the most.
Prop 123 money can buy land now for homes built later.
Workers here often earn too much for 60% rents and too little for market rents.
Often raised in resort towns. Colorado authority is unclear: read the status first.

job_centre.why: New market-rate building is steady here, so a share of it can be affordable.
Employers drive the need. Colorado authority for commercial linkage is unclear: read the status first.
Larger sites and deeper markets can carry a bond deal of 100+ homes.
The state credit closes much of the gap on a 4% bond deal.
More homes on the same site lowers the land cost per home.
Parking is a large cost per home where land is dear and transit is near.

growing.why: Buying land ahead of growth fixes its price before it rises.
Prop 123 money can buy land now for homes built later.
Much new building is coming, so a share of it can be affordable.
Prop 123 fast-track cuts time, and time is money on a growing market.
Growth supports larger rental deals that carry bond financing.
First-time buyers can still get in while prices are rising.

softening.why: Buying existing rentals while prices soften keeps them affordable for less than building.
Debt for buying and fixing existing affordable rentals.
Debt to buy or refinance existing apartments.
State money for buying and fixing homes outside the large cities.
Repairs lower the cost of living in homes people already have.
Homes bought while prices are low can stay affordable for good.

steady.why: The 9% credit is the usual route for a 30-60 home rental sized to local need.
State gap money that most tax credit deals in Colorado carry.
Waived fees lower the cost of every home a local deal builds.
Public land is often the largest local contribution a town can make.
Helps local renters buy where prices are steady.

no_rent_edge.label: No rent edge (benchmark)
no_rent_edge.rule: Benchmark only: the county HUD 2-bedroom Fair Market Rent is at or below the CHFA 60% AMI rent ceiling. A county FMR is not an achievable local lease rent; check observed rent comps for the site.

items.why: Rental assistance lets homes reach households well below 60% AMI.
Pays for homes at 30% AMI, where the real gap is.
Ownership can be the better buy where rents already sit near the limit.
Built for rentals of 5 to 19 homes.
Rural rental loans. Check the USDA eligibility map for the site.
State HOME money for places outside the large cities.

no_prop123.label: No Prop 123 commitment
no_prop123.rule: No filed Prop 123 commitment on the DOLA list for this town (or, for a county or CDP, this county).

items.why: Needs a filed commitment. Filing one opens this and DOLA homeownership grants.

ia:shared_equity_deed_restriction.name: Shared equity and deed-restriction buy-down
ia:shared_equity_deed_restriction.status_reason: SB24-174 lists acquiring or preserving deed restrictions on current housing units as a state-recognized affordable homeownership strategy, and C.R.S. 39-3-127.7 defines affordable homeownership property by deed restrictions that limit resale price or buyers.
ia:shared_equity_deed_restriction.what: The local government pays part of a home's price in exchange for a recorded deed restriction that caps resale price or limits buyers to income-qualified households.
ia:shared_equity_deed_restriction.quote: (III) ACQUIRING OR PRESERVING DEED RESTRICTIONS ON CURRENT HOUSING UNITS;

ia:lodging_or_str_tax.name: Lodging or short-term-rental tax for housing
ia:lodging_or_str_tax.status_reason: C.R.S. 30-11-107.5 lets a county levy a lodging tax of not more than two percent for purposes that include housing for the tourism-related workforce and other workers, with voter approval at a general election, and TABOR requires voter approval for any new tax.
ia:lodging_or_str_tax.what: A tax on hotel and short-term-rental stays whose revenue is used for workforce housing.
ia:lodging_or_str_tax.quote: the board of county commissioners of each county, for one or more of the purposes specified in subsection (1.5) of this section, may levy a county lodging tax of not more than two percent on the purchase price paid or charged to persons for rooms or accommodations

ia:land_bank_public_land.name: Land banking and public land for housing
ia:land_bank_public_land.status_reason: C.R.S. 29-20-104(1)(e.7)(IV) counts making surplus local-government property available for housing as a pro-housing action, and HB24-1175 gave local governments a right of first refusal or first offer on certain multifamily rental properties that terminates on December 31, 2029.
ia:land_bank_public_land.what: The local government acquires, holds or makes available land it owns for affordable housing, including a time-limited right to buy certain multifamily rental properties.
ia:land_bank_public_land.quote: Adopt policies to materially make surplus property owned by the local government available for the development of housing; or

fg:prop123-ahff-land-banking.name: Proposition 123 Land Banking Program
fg:prop123-ahff-land-banking.status_reason: OPEN for Rural and Rural Resort projects: rolling from September 15, 2026 through December 31, 2026 or until funds are exhausted ($16M). Open to all projects starting January 2027 ($16M plus any rural balance). Request an application by emailing landbanking@chfainfo.com.
fg:prop123-ahff-land-banking.what: Land acquisition for future affordable rental or for-sale housing (mixed use allowed if affordable housing is the predominant use).
fg:prop123-ahff-land-banking.quote: Lesser of $5 million or CHFA's concluded appraised value

fg:chfa-mihtc.name: Colorado Middle-income Housing Tax Credit (MIHTC)
fg:chfa-mihtc.status_reason: One competitive round (2026 application deadline May 18, 2026), then rolling applications while credit remains: applications due the first business day of August, September, October and November, with the LOI due the first business day of the month before. The only remaining 2026 rolling date is the first business day of November 2026 (LOI was due the first business day of October).
fg:chfa-mihtc.what: A stand-alone Colorado tax credit (not paired with federal LIHTC) for rental housing serving households from 80% to 120% AMI, or up to 140% AMI in rural resort counties. Pilot created by HB24-1316.
fg:chfa-mihtc.quote: CHFA will accept Applications for no less than $1,650,000 of MIHTC and up to $5,000,000 maximum

ia:vacancy_or_second_home_tax.name: Vacant-home or second-home tax
ia:vacancy_or_second_home_tax.status_reason: SB24-174 lists vacancy fees for underutilized units as a long-term strategy, but HB26-1036, which would have expressly authorized voter-approved local vacancy taxes, was Lost, and reporting says none has been implemented in Colorado.
ia:vacancy_or_second_home_tax.what: A tax or fee on residences left vacant or not used as a primary residence, with revenue for housing.
ia:vacancy_or_second_home_tax.quote: (b) REGULATING SHORT-TERM RENTALS, SECOND HOMES, OR OTHER UNDERUTILIZED OR VACANT UNITS IN A WAY, SUCH AS VACANCY FEES FOR UNDERUTILIZED UNITS, THAT PROMOTES A SUBSTANTIAL INCREASE IN THE USE OF LOCAL HOUSING STOCK FOR LOCAL HOUSING NEEDS;

ia:inclusionary_zoning_rental.name: Inclusionary zoning (rental, HB21-1117)
ia:inclusionary_zoning_rental.status_reason: C.R.S. 29-20-104(1)(e.5) exempts rent-restricting inclusionary regulations from the rent-control ban if they offer alternatives to on-site units, but (1)(e.7) requires the local government first to have taken one or more listed pro-housing actions.
ia:inclusionary_zoning_rental.what: New residential development must include a share of rent-restricted homes or choose an alternative such as a fee or off-site units.
ia:inclusionary_zoning_rental.quote: The provisions of section 38-12-301 shall not apply to any land use regulation adopted pursuant to this section that restricts rents on newly constructed or redeveloped housing units as long as the regulation provides a choice of options to the property owner or land developer and creates one or more alternatives to the construction of new affordable housing units on the building site.

ia:linkage_fee.name: Linkage fee (residential or commercial)
ia:linkage_fee.status_reason: State strategy directories in SB24-174 and HB24-1313 name a linkage fee on market-rate housing development as an example of a dedicated local revenue source, but no fetched statute expressly authorizes a commercial linkage fee.
ia:linkage_fee.what: A per-square-foot charge on new development that goes to affordable housing, tied to the housing demand the development creates.
ia:linkage_fee.quote: (a) ESTABLISHING A DEDICATED LOCAL REVENUE SOURCE FOR REGULATED AFFORDABLE HOUSING DEVELOPMENT, SUCH AS INSTITUTING A LINKAGE FEE ON MARKET RATE HOUSING DEVELOPMENT TO SUPPORT NEW, REGULATED AFFORDABLE HOUSING DEVELOPMENTS;

fg:chfa-federal-4pct-lihtc-pab.name: Federal 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credit with tax-exempt Private Activity Bonds (CHFA)
fg:chfa-federal-4pct-lihtc-pab.status_reason: Rolling. Bond-financed 4% applications are accepted all year except February, August and December. 2026 PAB Fund applications are due by 5:00pm MT on the first business day of April, May, July, September, October and November 2026; the last one is the first business day of November 2026. An LOI and concept meeting are required at least 45 days before the application.
fg:chfa-federal-4pct-lihtc-pab.what: Non-competitive federal credit equity for rental projects financed with tax-exempt private activity bonds. The credit sits outside the 9% state ceiling but depends on getting bond volume cap.
fg:chfa-federal-4pct-lihtc-pab.quote: Except for projects financed with Private Activity Bonds, CHFA will accept Applications for no more than $1,800,000

fg:chfa-colorado-state-ahtc.name: Colorado State Affordable Housing Tax Credit (state LIHTC: standard and accelerated)
fg:chfa-colorado-state-ahtc.status_reason: Round One (with 9%) and Round Two (with 4%). The 2026 Round Two application closed August 3, 2026. Under the adopted QAP, 4% bond projects may request state credit in September, October and November 2026 as available. Next competitive round: 2027 Round One (LOI December 1, 2026, per the not-yet-adopted 2027-28 draft).
fg:chfa-colorado-state-ahtc.what: A Colorado income tax credit, claimed over six years and paired with a federal housing tax credit, that adds equity to LIHTC rental projects. Standard credit goes with 9% deals in Round One; accelerated credit goes with 4% bond deals in Round Two.
fg:chfa-colorado-state-ahtc.quote: CHFA will pair, if requested, a fixed amount of $500,000 of standard annual state credit with federal 9 percent Housing Tax Credit Applications.

ia:density_bonus.name: Density bonus
ia:density_bonus.status_reason: C.R.S. 29-20-104(1)(e.7)(I)(G) lists granting density bonuses to projects that include affordable units as a qualifying pro-housing action, and SB24-174 lists a density bonus program as a standard affordability strategy.
ia:density_bonus.what: Projects that include affordable units may build more units, floor area or height than zoning otherwise allows.
ia:density_bonus.quote: Granting density bonuses to development projects that incorporate affordable housing units; or

ia:parking_reduction.name: Parking requirement reduction
ia:parking_reduction.status_reason: C.R.S. 29-20-104(1)(e.7)(I)(F) lists reduced parking for housing near transit or affordable developments as a pro-housing action, and HB24-1304 bars local governments in metropolitan planning organizations from enforcing minimum parking on multifamily development in transit service areas.
ia:parking_reduction.what: Lower or remove minimum off-street parking requirements for housing, especially affordable or transit-adjacent projects.
ia:parking_reduction.quote: Granting reduced parking requirements to residential or mixed-use developments that include housing near transit stations or affordable housing developments;

ia:expedited_review.name: Expedited review (Prop 123 fast-track)
ia:expedited_review.status_reason: C.R.S. 29-32-105(2)(a) requires a local government that commits under Prop 123 to give a final decision within ninety calendar days of a complete application for projects where fifty percent or more of units are affordable.
ia:expedited_review.what: Development applications for mostly affordable projects get a final decision on a guaranteed short timeline.
ia:expedited_review.quote: must establish processes to enable it to provide a final decision on any application for a special permit, variance, or other development permit, excluding subdivisions, of a development project for which fifty percent or more of the residential units in the development constitute affordable housing not more than ninety calendar days after submission of a complete application, referred to herein as a "fast-track approval process."

ho:chfa-dpa-grant.name: CHFA Down Payment Assistance Grant
ho:chfa-dpa-grant.what: CHFA borrowers may pair a CHFA first mortgage with grant help for down payment or closing costs. The grant does not have to be repaid, but borrowers must qualify through a CHFA participating lender.
ho:chfa-dpa-grant.quote: CHFA lists a grant up to the lesser of $25,000 or 3% of the first mortgage, with no repayment required.

fg:chfa-cahp-preservation-fund.name: Colorado Affordable Housing Preservation Fund (CAHP) loan
fg:chfa-cahp-preservation-fund.status_reason: Open; 30 to 60 days processing from complete application to commitment.
fg:chfa-cahp-preservation-fund.what: Second-mortgage acquisition financing up to $1 million to preserve existing subsidized or naturally occurring affordable rentals of 5 to 100 units at risk of losing affordability.

fg:freddie-mac-tah.name: Freddie Mac Multifamily Optigo Targeted Affordable Housing (TAH)
fg:freddie-mac-tah.what: Loans for properties affordable to low and very-low income families: cash loans, bond credit enhancement with 4% LIHTC, tax-exempt loans, 9% LIHTC cash loans, preservation rehab, HUD Section 8 and USDA Section 515 financing, lease-up and bridge loans.
fg:freddie-mac-tah.quote: loans for properties in underserved areas that are affordable to families with low and very-low incomes including cash loans, bond credit enhancements, tax-exempt loans, and others.

fg:hud-223f.name: HUD/FHA Section 207/223(f) Mortgage Insurance (acquisition or refinance of existing rental housing)
fg:hud-223f.what: FHA insurance on loans to buy or refinance existing multifamily rental housing; non-critical repairs allowed, substantial rehabilitation not allowed.
fg:hud-223f.quote: Section 207/223(f) insures mortgage loans to facilitate the purchase or refinancing of existing multifamily rental housing.

fg:doh-cdbg-housing.name: DOH Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Housing, non-entitlement areas
fg:doh-cdbg-housing.status_reason: Offered in the July 2026 development round (applications due July 30, 2026). A separate 2026 CDBG Abatement and Demolition NOFA is posted. No later development round is published.
fg:doh-cdbg-housing.what: Housing-related activities in smaller communities: infrastructure for housing projects, rental acquisition and rehab, down payment assistance, owner-occupied rehab, abatement and demolition.
fg:doh-cdbg-housing.quote: Rental and Homeownership 51 percent of units must serve Low- to Moderate-Income households up to 80% AMI

ho:colorado-wap-weatherization.name: Colorado Weatherization Assistance Program
ho:colorado-wap-weatherization.what: WAP can help income-qualified homeowners and renters reduce energy costs through local weatherization services. Colorado delivery runs through state and local providers, so eligibility and timing must be confirmed before a household plans work.
ho:colorado-wap-weatherization.quote: DOE says WAP is state/local administered and eligible households may apply through local providers; homeowners and renters can be eligible.

ia:community_land_trust.name: Community land trust
ia:community_land_trust.status_reason: C.R.S. 39-3-127.7 exempts qualifying land held by a community land trust and leased to the owner of an affordable homeownership property from property tax for tax years from January 1, 2024, and SB24-174 lists local programs for land banking or community land trusts as a strategy.
ia:community_land_trust.what: A nonprofit keeps ownership of the land and sells or leases the homes on it at restricted prices so they stay affordable from one owner to the next.
ia:community_land_trust.quote: "Community land trust" means a nonprofit organization that is exempt from taxation under section 501 (c)(3) of the federal "Internal Revenue Code of 1986", as amended, and is designed to ensure long-term housing affordability through a shared-equity model

fg:chfa-federal-9pct-lihtc.name: Federal 9% Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (CHFA competitive Round One)
fg:chfa-federal-9pct-lihtc.status_reason: One competitive round per year (Round One, 9% plus standard state credit). The 2026 round closed February 2, 2026. Next: 2027 Round One letter of intent due December 1, 2026 and application due February 1, 2027 by 5:00pm MT, per section 3.B.2 of the adopted 2027-28 QAP.
fg:chfa-federal-9pct-lihtc.what: Equity for new construction, acquisition and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing. Investors buy the 10-year federal credit; CHFA awards it competitively under its Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP).
fg:chfa-federal-9pct-lihtc.quote: CHFA will accept Applications for no more than $1,800,000 of the annual federal 9 percent Housing Tax Credit for any one project or any one Applicant

fg:doh-housing-development-grant.name: DOH Housing Development Grant Fund (HDG)
fg:doh-housing-development-grant.status_reason: Quarterly competitive rounds, $8-11 million each. October 2026: application due October 15, 2026 (LOI was due August 31, 2026). January 2027: LOI December 1, 2026; application January 15, 2027. April 2027: LOI March 16, 2027; application April 30, 2027.
fg:doh-housing-development-grant.what: Acquisition, rehabilitation and new construction of affordable rental and for-sale housing and mobile home parks.

ia:fee_waiver_reduction.name: Fee waiver or reduction for affordable housing
ia:fee_waiver_reduction.status_reason: C.R.S. 29-20-104.5(5) expressly lets a local government waive an impact fee or similar development charge on low- or moderate-income or affordable employee housing as it defines it.
ia:fee_waiver_reduction.what: The local government waives or lowers impact fees and other development charges on income-restricted homes.
ia:fee_waiver_reduction.quote: a local government may impose an impact fee or other similar development charge to fund expenditures by such local government or a fire and emergency services provider that provides fire protection, rescue, and emergency services in the new development on capital facilities needed to serve new development. No impact fee or other similar development charge shall be imposed except pursuant to a schedule that is: (a)Legislatively adopted; (b)Generally applicable to a broad class of property; and (c)Intended to defray the projected impacts on capital facilities caused by proposed development.

fg:hud-pbv.name: Project-Based Vouchers (Housing Choice Voucher program, 24 CFR part 983)
fg:hud-pbv.status_reason: Set by each PHA's selection process (competitive or allowed non-competitive selection).
fg:hud-pbv.what: A PHA attaches Housing Choice Voucher assistance to specific units under a Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) contract with the owner.
fg:hud-pbv.quote: a PHA may commit project-based assistance to no more than 20 percent of its authorized voucher units

fg:doh-national-housing-trust-fund.name: DOH National Housing Trust Fund (HTF)
fg:doh-national-housing-trust-fund.status_reason: Offered in the July 2026 round with CDBG and HOME (about $10 million federal; applications due July 30, 2026). No later HTF round is published.
fg:doh-national-housing-trust-fund.what: New construction, acquisition and rehabilitation of rental housing for extremely low-income households.
fg:doh-national-housing-trust-fund.quote: Rental Housing development with all DOH-assisted units restricted to 30% AMI or lower

fg:prop123-dola-affordable-homeownership.name: Proposition 123 Affordable Homeownership Program (AHOP): New Construction / Acquisition Rehabilitation
fg:prop123-dola-affordable-homeownership.status_reason: Competitive DOH rounds. October 2026 round: LOI due August 31, 2026, application due October 15, 2026 ($6-8M homeownership development). January 2027 round: LOI December 1, 2026, application January 15, 2027. April 2027 round: LOI March 16, 2027, application April 30, 2027. The 2026 Scattered-Site Homeownership NOFA ($30M) closed with applications due July 30, 2026.
fg:prop123-dola-affordable-homeownership.what: Grants for affordable for-sale housing: new construction, acquisition/rehab of homes, land acquisition, plus predevelopment grants. AHOP also funds down payment assistance, mobile home and owner-occupied rehab programs run by partners.

fg:chfa-small-scale-perm-loan.name: CHFA Small-scale Housing Permanent Loan (5 to 19 units)
fg:chfa-small-scale-perm-loan.status_reason: Open; 60 to 90 days from complete application to commitment.
fg:chfa-small-scale-perm-loan.what: Uninsured permanent loan up to $2.5 million for new construction, acq/rehab or refinance of 5- to 19-unit rental properties.

fg:usda-515.name: USDA Rural Development Section 515 Multifamily Housing Direct Loans
fg:usda-515.status_reason: Closed as of 2026-10-10; applications accepted only after a NOFA/NOSA is published in the Federal Register.
fg:usda-515.what: Direct, competitive loans for construction, improvement and purchase of affordable multifamily rental housing for low-income, elderly or disabled households in eligible rural areas, plus land and infrastructure.
fg:usda-515.quote: This program provides competitive financing for affordable multi-family rental housing for low-income, elderly, or disabled individuals and families in eligible rural areas.

fg:doh-home.name: DOH HOME Investment Partnerships Program (State, balance of state)
fg:doh-home.status_reason: Federal funds (CDBG, HOME, HTF) were offered at about $10 million in the July 2026 round (applications due July 30, 2026). HOME CHDO Operating (~$300,000) in January 2027 round (LOI December 1, 2026; application January 15, 2027). No later HOME development round is published.
fg:doh-home.what: Rental acquisition, rehabilitation and construction; homebuyer assistance; owner-occupied rehab; CHDO set-aside and operating funds.

fg:prop123-ahff-lihtc-gap.name: Proposition 123 Concessionary Debt: LIHTC Gap Finance
fg:prop123-ahff-lihtc-gap.status_reason: Last round ran May 27 to June 10, 2026. FY2027 plan: $44M of LIHTC Gap reserved for competitive Housing Tax Credit applicants under the 2027-2028 QAP (up to $25M in 2027 Round One, up to $19M in Round Two); a small amount in open Concessionary Debt rounds opening October 2026 and February 2027 for emergency needs. The October 2026 round takes applications October 21 to November 10, 2026 (5:00pm MT), with selections in December 2026, per CHFA's October 19, 2026 notice.
fg:prop123-ahff-lihtc-gap.what: Subordinate gap loans for affordable rental projects that have a federal Low Income Housing Tax Credit award but have not converted to permanent financing.
fg:prop123-ahff-lihtc-gap.quote: Starting Wednesday, October 21st, applications and supporting materials will be accepted for the Proposition 123 Concessionary Debt Multifamily Finance, LIHTC Gap Finance, and LIHTC Predevelopment Finance loan options

meta.menu_note: Menu items are our reading of what tends to fit each type, not advice for any one site. Each names a program or tool from a cited record; check its own terms before relying on it.

validation.stability: Stability under seasonal-share uncertainty: the share of 500 redraws of the ACS seasonal share (from its margin of error) in which a place keeps its pattern. Jobs, growth and the market call are not redrawn.

cluster_check.method: k-means, 5 groups, 20 starts, on standardised seasonal share (log), jobs per working resident (log) and household growth
cluster_check.reading: Agreement between the written types and groups found without them (0 is chance, 1 is the same grouping).

limits: Rent edge compares the county HUD 2BR Fair Market Rent with the CHFA 60% AMI rent ceiling. It is a benchmark, not an achievable lease rent: use observed rent comps for a site.
A COHO market pattern is not CHFA's urban, rural or mountain property category.
Jobs and residents are LODES primary jobs for 2023, inside Colorado only.
Seasonal homes are ACS 5-year estimates; small places carry wide margins (see stability).
A pattern describes the market, not the right answer for a site.
